title: What has maths got to do with the world around us?
description: A village at dusk, a home, a school, a market and a game show things that come back again and again. The video ends on the open question of what mathematics is really about.
teaching_notes: One idea: the world is full of things that repeat, and mathematics has something to say about them. Ask children to guess, and do not confirm any guess, because the next topic settles it. Watch for students who think maths is only sums.

source: What comes next in the matchstick row?
video_script.why: Before any definition, the child sees that something repeats all around us and wonders what mathematics has to do with it.
video_script.substitution: Picture the sky, a home, a school, a market and a game, each with something that repeats, and ask what maths is about.
video_script.anchor: the Sun and Moon over a village, then a home, a school, a market and a game, from the opening page of the book
hold_back: mathematics is the search for patterns
maths_rules: No number, formula or answer is shown.
The book's opening: patterns exist in nature, homes and schools, in the motion of the Sun and Moon, in shopping, cooking, throwing a ball, games, weather and technology.
The open question: what does mathematics have to do with all this. It is never answered here.
video_script.design: One idea: things repeat all around us. Assumes nothing. Wrong idea: none is broken. The scenes join one by one and all stay to the end.
open_questions: The worklist title mentions a matchstick row, but the book text has no matchsticks, so this opener follows the book's own opening section instead. The old photo ph_matchstick_row is no longer shown by any video.
